title: Floaters

description.main: Floaters is a 2014 photobook by Mayumi Hosokura, published by Waterfall in Taipei in an edition of 500. Colour film shot during a 2012 residency at the Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts was reprinted as tintypes, scanned and output as C-prints, keeping the bubbles, drips and scratches of the process. The 80-page softcover comes in a PVC sleeve and includes a short story by Yen Shuxia in Chinese, Japanese and English.
description.extended:
Floaters is a photobook by Mayumi Hosokura, published by Waterfall in Taipei in 2014, that reprints colour film shot in Taiwan as tintypes, so that silhouettes of heads, bodies and foliage come through in blue and grey, marked by bubbles, drips and scratches.

Hosokura began the series in 2012 during a residency at the Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts in Taipei. She shot colour film, printed it as tintypes on handmade plates, then scanned the plates for C-prints, leaving every flaw of the process in. Waterfall issued the book in November 2014 as an 80-page softcover in a PVC sleeve, 19 by 29.5 cm, offset printed in an edition of 500. The pictures appear in two versions, with extracts from the artist's diary and test sheets from the printer bound in as interleaves. A short story, Lost, by the Taiwanese writer Yen Shuxia, runs in Chinese, Japanese and English. The series was shown at G/P gallery in Tokyo in 2013.

Hosokura was born in Kyoto in 1979 and lives in Tokyo. Floaters followed Kazan (Artbeat Publishers, 2012) and came out the same year as Crystal Love Starlight (Tycoon Books, 2014). Her later books include Transparency Is the New Mystery (MACK, 2016) and New Skin (MACK, 2019). She is represented by Takuro Someya Contemporary Art in Tokyo.
description.artist_bio: Mayumi Hosokura (b. 1979, Kyoto) lives and works in Tokyo. Degrees in literature (Ritsumeikan University, 2002) and photography (Nihon University College of Art, 2005). Foam Talent 2011. Books: Kazan (Artbeat, 2012), Floaters (Waterfall, 2014), Crystal Love Starlight (Tycoon Books, 2014), Transparency Is the New Mystery (MACK, 2016), Jubilee (2017), New Skin (MACK, 2019). Represented by Takuro Someya Contemporary Art, Tokyo.
description.exhibition_context: Series begun during a 2012 artist residency at Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts, Taipei (where she showed Transparency is the new mystery, 2012); Floaters shown as a solo exhibition at G/P gallery, Tokyo, 2013 (artist CV).

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Cover carries the Chinese title 浮游物 (Waterfall is a Taipei publisher); the English title Floaters is printed on the PVC sleeve. Edition of 500. Short story "Lost" by Yen Shuxia (言叔夏), translated by Stephen Ma; printer's test sheets bound in as interleaves.
